meta.title: Manoeuvring and position on the carriageway
meta.summary: You will learn how to signal, change lanes, turn, make U-turns and reverse correctly. You will find out which lane to use on different roads and what following distance to keep.

p: Every manoeuvre starts with a signal: this way others understand in advance what you are going to do. Signals are given with the direction indicators or, if there are none or they are faulty, by hand. The manoeuvre itself must be safe and must not impede others ⟦18⟧.
In the Rules, a manoeuvre is not only a turn. Moving off from a standstill, stopping, changing lanes, braking and reversing also count as manoeuvring ⟦19⟧.
list: Left: the left direction indicator, or the left arm extended to the side, or the right arm extended to the side and bent upwards at the elbow at a right angle.
Right: the right direction indicator, or the right arm extended to the side, or the left arm extended to the side and bent upwards at the elbow at a right angle.
Braking: the brake lights or a raised arm. Reversing: the reversing lights and the hazard warning lights.
A signal is given in good time and in a way that does not mislead others, and it is cancelled immediately after the manoeuvre. A hand signal may be ended immediately before the manoeuvre ⟦20⟧.
lesson.tip: A signal is a warning, not a right. It does not give you priority or release you from taking precautions ⟦21⟧.

lesson.h: Entering and leaving a road, yards, acceleration and deceleration lanes
list: When pulling out from a minor road onto a road, give way to vehicles and pedestrians moving along the road you are entering ⟦22⟧.
A dirt road is a minor road in relation to a paved road, even if there are no signs ⟦23⟧.
When leaving a residential zone or a yard, give way to all other road users ⟦24⟧.
When leaving a road, give way to vehicles and pedestrians whose path you cross ⟦25⟧.
When approaching a place to stop or park, give way to pedestrians, cyclists, drivers of mopeds and horse-drawn carts, and drovers moving along the edge of the carriageway or on the shoulder ⟦26⟧.
If there is a deceleration lane, move into it in good time and slow down only in that lane ⟦27⟧.
If there is an acceleration lane, drive along it and move into the adjacent lane, giving way to vehicles travelling on the road ⟦28⟧.

p: When you change lanes, you move into another stream of traffic. That is why those driving straight on in their own lane have priority.
list: Give way to vehicles travelling in the same direction that are not changing lanes ⟦29⟧.
If you and a vehicle alongside change lanes at the same time, the driver who has the other vehicle on the right gives way ⟦30⟧.
You must not change lanes in a way that leaves a dangerous distance between vehicles ⟦31⟧.
If the lanes are marked, keep strictly to them. You may drive over broken marking lines only when changing lanes ⟦32⟧.
If paths cross and the Rules do not specify who goes first, the driver who has the other vehicle approaching from the right gives way ⟦33⟧.
lesson.tip: When vehicles change lanes at the same time, the driver with the other vehicle on the right gives way.

p: Before turning right or left or making a U-turn, take up the appropriate far right or far left position on the carriageway in advance ⟦34⟧. The exception is a turn made when entering a roundabout.
Turn in such a way that, on leaving the intersection of the carriageways, you do not end up on the side for oncoming traffic ⟦35⟧.
list: If signs 5.8.1 or 5.8.2 are installed, turn from the lanes they permit. However, you must not take an inner lane while the far lane on the side of the turn is free ⟦36⟧.

If there are tram tracks for the same direction on the left, level with the road, and signs 5.8.1 or 5.8.2 do not set lane directions, you turn left and make U-turns from the tram tracks, giving way to trams ⟦37⟧.

If your vehicle cannot turn from the far right or far left position because of its dimensions, you may move partly or completely into the adjacent lane, provided this is safe and does not impede anyone ⟦38⟧.

p: The arrows of marking 1.18 and signs 5.8.1 and 5.8.2 show which way you may go from each lane. If the arrow in your lane points straight ahead only, you must not turn from that lane, even when the adjacent lane is free.

A turn is made into the lane that corresponds to the one you occupy (para. 53, in force since 6 May 2024): from the far right lane into the far right lane, from the far left into the far left, from the second into the second. You may change lanes once the turn is complete. A special case is turning onto a road with reversible traffic: there you take the far right lane straight away ⟦39⟧.
list: A left arrow in the far left lane also permits a U-turn from that lane (marking 1.18, signs 5.8.1, 5.8.2).
Does a sign permit turning from several lanes? Do not take an inner lane while the far lane on the side of the turn is free ⟦40⟧.
Marking 1.18 showing a dead end means that turning into the nearest carriageway is prohibited.
lesson.tip: The “lane-to-lane” rule appeared in 2024, so older question banks may not include it.

p: You may make a U-turn with any turning radius, provided it is safe and does not impede others ⟦41⟧. Outside an intersection, when turning left or making a U-turn, give way to oncoming vehicles ⟦42⟧.

If the road is narrow and a U-turn from the far left position is not possible, the U-turn may be made only from the right edge of the carriageway (from the right-hand shoulder), and you give way to vehicles travelling in the same direction as well as to oncoming vehicles ⟦43⟧.
list: on pedestrian crossings, including at intersections along the line of the pavements or shoulders where pedestrians cross (U-turns at the intersection itself are not prohibited, para. 61);
in tunnels;
on bridges, overpasses and flyovers, and under them;
on level crossings;
where visibility of the road is less than 100 m;
at bus (tram) stops.
lesson.tip: On motorways, U-turns, entering service gaps in the central reservation and reversing are prohibited ⟦45⟧. Sign 5.11.1 “U-turn place” shows where you may make a U-turn, but turning left there is prohibited.

p: Visibility is worst to the rear, so reversing is permitted only if it is safe and does not impede others ⟦46⟧. Reversing is signalled by the reversing lights and the hazard warning lights ⟦47⟧.
list: Reversing is prohibited at intersections.

Reversing is prohibited wherever U-turns are prohibited: on pedestrian crossings, in tunnels, on bridges, overpasses and flyovers and under them, on level crossings, where visibility is less than 100 m, and at stops ⟦48⟧.
lesson.tip: Missed the turning you needed at an intersection? Do not reverse: drive on to a place where you can legally make a U-turn.

lesson.h: How many lanes there are and where the oncoming side is
p: The number of lanes is shown by road markings or signs 5.8.1, 5.8.2, 5.8.7 and 5.8.8. If there are none, drivers determine it themselves, taking into account the width of the carriageway, the dimensions of the vehicles and the necessary clearances ⟦49⟧.
The left half of the carriageway is considered the side for oncoming traffic, unless traffic management establishes otherwise. Local widening of the road is not taken into account ⟦50⟧.
list: Two-way traffic, four or more lanes: driving onto the side for oncoming traffic is prohibited. Left turns and U-turns are made at intersections and in other places where they are not prohibited ⟦51⟧.
Two-way traffic, three lanes: driving into the far left lane, which is intended for oncoming traffic, is prohibited ⟦52⟧.
Two-way traffic, two lanes separated by marking 1.1 and (or) marked with sign 3.20: driving onto the oncoming side is prohibited, except in cases provided for by the Rules ⟦53⟧.

p: Kazakhstan has right-hand traffic ⟦54⟧. Outside built-up areas, and also in towns on roads with signs 5.1 and 5.3 or where more than 80 km/h is permitted, keep close to the right edge and do not use the left lanes while the right lanes are free ⟦55⟧.

In built-up areas, you may drive in any lane. But if you are driving in the left lane slower than the permitted speed, and a faster vehicle approaches from behind giving a warning light signal (flashing its headlights by day or switching between dipped and main-beam headlights at night, para. 140), move to the right and free the lane ⟦56⟧.
list: Three or more lanes in one direction: the far left lane is used only in heavy traffic, when the other lanes are occupied, and also for overtaking, turning left or making a U-turn ⟦57⟧.
On such roads, trucks with a maximum authorised mass of more than 3500 kg may use the far left lane only for turning left or making a U-turn ⟦58⟧.
On motorways, trucks with a maximum authorised mass of more than 3500 kg must not drive beyond the second lane ⟦59⟧.

Vehicles that travel at no more than 40 km/h or cannot technically reach that speed keep to the far right lane. Exceptions: driving around an obstacle, overtaking, and changing lanes before turning left, making a U-turn or making a permitted stop on the left-hand side ⟦60⟧.
Driving in your own lane faster than vehicles in the adjacent lane is not overtaking ⟦61⟧, so sign 3.20 does not prohibit it.

lesson.h: Tram tracks, shoulders and obstacles in the middle of the road
list: You may drive on tram tracks for the same direction, on the left and level with the road, when all lanes are occupied, and also when driving around an obstacle, overtaking, turning left or making a U-turn. You must not impede trams ⟦62⟧.
You must not drive onto tram tracks for the oncoming direction. If signs 5.8.1 or 5.8.2 are installed, you must not drive through the intersection on the tram tracks ⟦63⟧.

Driving on shoulders, pavements and footpaths is prohibited, and in built-up areas driving off the carriageway, for example on lawns, is prohibited too. Exceptions: road maintenance and utility vehicles, and vehicles delivering goods that approach by the shortest route when there is no other access ⟦64⟧.
Traffic islands, bollards and bridge supports in the middle of a road without a central reservation are driven around on the right, unless signs and markings require otherwise ⟦65⟧.
Having turned onto a road with reversible traffic, take the far right lane. Change lanes only after making sure that driving in your direction is also permitted in the other lanes ⟦66⟧.

p: The following distance is the distance to the vehicle in front. Keep a distance that lets you avoid a collision if it brakes sharply. The higher the speed, the greater the distance you need. The lateral clearance to vehicles alongside must also be safe ⟦67⟧.

Outside built-up areas, on two-lane roads with two-way traffic, vehicles for which a speed limit has been set, and vehicles or vehicle combinations longer than 7 m, keep enough distance ahead for overtaking vehicles to return to their lane without hindrance. This is not required if the driver is preparing to overtake, in heavy traffic or in an organised convoy ⟦68⟧.
lesson.tip: Paragraph 69 does not give an exact figure in metres: a safe distance depends on the speed and the situation.

keyFacts: A signal is given in good time and cancelled immediately after the manoeuvre; it does not give priority ⟦1⟧.
Right-turn hand signal: the right arm extended to the side, or the left arm bent upwards at the elbow at a right angle; braking: a raised arm ⟦2⟧.
When changing lanes, give way to vehicles travelling in the same direction without changing lanes; when changing lanes at the same time, give way to the one on the right ⟦3⟧.
Before turning or making a U-turn, take up the far right or far left position in advance, and turn into the lane that corresponds to the one you occupy ⟦4⟧.
A left arrow in the far left lane (marking 1.18, signs 5.8.1, 5.8.2) also permits a U-turn.

Outside an intersection, when turning left or making a U-turn, give way to oncoming vehicles; when making a U-turn from the right-hand shoulder, give way both to vehicles travelling in the same direction and to oncoming vehicles ⟦5⟧.
U-turns are prohibited on pedestrian crossings, in tunnels, on bridges, overpasses and flyovers and under them, on level crossings, where visibility is less than 100 m, and at stops ⟦6⟧.
Reversing is prohibited at intersections and wherever U-turns are prohibited; it is signalled by the reversing lights and the hazard warning lights ⟦7⟧.
When leaving a yard or a residential zone, give way to everyone; when pulling out from a dirt road onto a paved road, give way to everyone travelling on it ⟦8⟧.
On a two-way road with 4 or more lanes, driving onto the oncoming side is prohibited; on a three-lane road, you must not use the far left lane ⟦9⟧.
Outside built-up areas and where more than 80 km/h is permitted, keep to the right; for trucks over 3500 kg, the far left of three lanes is only for turning left and making U-turns ⟦10⟧.
Vehicles and vehicle combinations longer than 7 m, and vehicles for which a speed limit has been set, leave room ahead for overtaking vehicles on a two-lane road outside built-up areas ⟦11⟧.
mistakes: Thinking that switching on your indicator gives you the right to change lanes. A signal does not give priority: give way to those driving straight on in the lane ⟦12⟧.
Turning right directly into the second lane, or turning left into the right lane. A turn is made into the lane that corresponds to the one you occupy ⟦13⟧.
Reversing at an intersection after overshooting your turning. Reversing at intersections is prohibited ⟦14⟧.
Making a U-turn on or under a bridge, at a stop or on a stretch where visibility is less than 100 m. All of this is prohibited ⟦15⟧.
Driving in the left lane of an out-of-town highway while the right lane is free. Outside built-up areas, you must keep to the right ⟦16⟧.
Driving around a traffic jam on the shoulder. Driving on shoulders is prohibited, except in cases expressly specified in the Rules ⟦17⟧.

questions.q: You have turned right into a new street. When must you switch off the direction indicator?
options: 50-100 m after the turn
Immediately after completing the manoeuvre
When you reach the next intersection
You need not switch it off if there is another right turn ahead
questions.explain: A signal is given in good time before the manoeuvre begins and cancelled immediately after it is completed. An indicator left on misleads other road users.

questions.q: A car's direction indicators are not working. The driver has put their left arm out of the window and bent it upwards at the elbow at a right angle. What is the driver signalling?
options: A left turn
Braking
A stop to pick up a passenger
A right turn
questions.explain: The signal for a manoeuvre to the right is the right arm extended to the side, or the left arm extended to the side and bent upwards at the elbow at a right angle. Braking is shown by a raised arm.

questions.q: You have switched on the left direction indicator to move into the left lane. Another car is travelling in that lane in the same direction without changing lanes. Who must give way?
options: You: a turn signal gives no priority
The car in the left lane: you signalled first
The one driving more slowly
The one further to the left
questions.explain: When changing lanes, a driver gives way to vehicles travelling in the same direction without changing direction. A switched-on direction indicator does not give priority.

questions.q: You are driving in the left lane of a road with three lanes in one direction and moving into the middle lane. At the same time, a green car is moving into the middle lane from the right lane. Who gives way?
options: The green car: you are on its left
The one driving faster
You: the green car is on your right
The one who switched on the indicator later
questions.explain: When vehicles travelling in the same direction change lanes at the same time, the driver gives way to the vehicle on the right. Here the green car is on your right, so you give way.

questions.q: You are turning right off the road into a yard. Pedestrians are walking across the pavement you are crossing. What should you do?
options: Go first: pedestrians must let the car through
Give way to pedestrians whose path you cross
Sound the horn and drive slowly between them
Give way only to pedestrians with children
questions.explain: When leaving a road, a driver gives way to vehicles and pedestrians whose path they cross.

questions.q: On your left there are tram tracks for the same direction, level with the carriageway. There are no signs 5.8.1 or 5.8.2. You want to turn left at the intersection. Where should you turn from?
options: From the tram tracks, giving way to the tram
From the left lane of the carriageway, without entering the tracks
From the right lane, after letting everyone go first
From the tram tracks: the tram must give way to you
questions.explain: If there are tram tracks for the same direction on the left, level with the road, and signs 5.8.1 or 5.8.2 do not set lane directions, left turns and U-turns are made from these tracks. In doing so, the driver gives way to trams.

questions.q: You want to make a U-turn outside an intersection, but the road is narrow and a U-turn from the far left position is not possible. What should you do?
options: Turn from the far left position, giving way only to oncoming vehicles
Turn from the left-hand shoulder, giving way only to vehicles going your way
Turn from the middle of the road, with the hazard warning lights on
Turn from the right-hand shoulder, giving way to vehicles going both ways
questions.explain: If the carriageway is too narrow for a U-turn from the far left position outside an intersection, the U-turn may be made only from the right edge (from the right-hand shoulder), and the driver gives way to vehicles travelling in the same direction and to oncoming vehicles.

questions.q: In which of these places is a U-turn permitted if there are no prohibitory signs or markings?
options: Under an overpass where visibility is good
At the location of a bus stop
On a straight road with 300 m visibility
In a tunnel with good lighting
questions.explain: U-turns are prohibited on pedestrian crossings, in tunnels, on bridges, overpasses and flyovers and under them, on level crossings, where visibility is less than 100 m, and at bus (tram) stops. A straight road with 300 m visibility is not on this list.

questions.q: You have driven past the turning you need at an intersection. May you reverse a little to make the turn?
options: No, reversing at intersections is prohibited
Yes, if you switch on the hazard warning lights
Yes, if there are no vehicles behind you
Yes, but no more than 5 m
questions.explain: Reversing is prohibited at intersections and in places where U-turns are prohibited. Drive on to a place where you can make a U-turn safely and legally.

questions.q: You are about to turn right, and a deceleration lane begins before the turn. Where should you slow down?
options: In the main lane, then move into the deceleration lane
Move into the deceleration lane in good time and slow down only there
During the turn itself
The deceleration lane is for trucks only; cars may brake in the main lane
questions.explain: Where there is a deceleration lane, a driver intending to turn moves into it in good time and slows down only in that lane. This way you do not hold up the traffic in the main lane.

questions.q: You are driving on a two-way road with two lanes in each direction. There is a slow truck ahead, and the left lane in your direction is occupied. May you overtake the truck using the oncoming side?
options: Yes, if the oncoming side is clear for 300 m
Yes, if there is no solid line 1.1 on the road
Yes, if you do not exceed 90 km/h while overtaking
No: you must not enter the oncoming side here
questions.explain: There are two lanes in each direction here, four in total. On such roads, driving onto the side for oncoming traffic is prohibited whatever the markings, so wait until the left lane in your direction is free.

questions.q: You are driving outside a built-up area on a road with three lanes in your direction. Traffic is light, and you are not overtaking anyone or turning. Which lane should you use?
options: The far left lane: it is the fastest
Any lane: the choice is the driver's
The far right lane, close to the right edge
The middle lane, so as not to impede those leaving the road
questions.explain: Outside built-up areas, vehicles are driven close to the right edge, and the left lanes are not used while the right lanes are free. The far left lane is used only in heavy traffic, for overtaking, turning left or making a U-turn.

questions.q: You are driving in town in the left lane, slower than the permitted speed. A faster car is approaching from behind and giving a warning signal. What should you do?
options: Carry on: in town you may drive in any lane
Move to the right and free the lane
Speed up beyond the permitted speed so as not to hold it up
Slow down so that it drops back
questions.explain: In built-up areas, you may drive in any lane, but a driver travelling in the left lane slower than the permitted speed must free it by moving to the right for a vehicle approaching from behind at a higher speed and giving warning signals.

questions.q: A truck with a maximum authorised mass of 12 t is travelling on a road with three lanes in one direction. When may it use the far left lane?
options: Only to turn left or make a U-turn
For overtaking and in heavy traffic
At any time, if the lane is free
Never
questions.explain: On roads with three or more lanes in one direction, trucks with a maximum authorised mass of more than 3500 kg may use the far left lane only to turn left or make a U-turn.

questions.q: You are stuck in a traffic jam in town. On the right there is a clear shoulder along which you could reach the turning you need. May you do this?
options: Yes, if you switch on the hazard warning lights
Yes, if you drive no faster than 20 km/h
No, driving on shoulders is prohibited
Yes, if there are no pedestrians on the shoulder
questions.explain: Driving vehicles on shoulders, pavements and footpaths is prohibited, except in cases expressly provided for by the Rules. Driving around a traffic jam is not one of them.

questions.q: You are driving a car with a trailer (the combination is 9 m long) on a two-lane out-of-town road with two-way traffic. Traffic is light, and you do not intend to overtake. What distance should you keep to the vehicle in front?
options: The minimum, so that nobody overtakes you
At least 50 m, whatever your speed
Any distance: for combinations, only lateral clearance matters
Enough for an overtaking car to pull in ahead of you
questions.explain: Your combination is longer than 7 m, you are not preparing to overtake, and traffic is light. In this case, outside built-up areas on a two-lane road, you keep enough distance ahead for overtaking vehicles to move back into the lane they occupied before without hindrance.

questions.q: There are no signs or markings that set lane directions. You are driving in the right lane. On which paths may you drive through the intersection?
options: Path B only
Paths A and B
Paths B and C
Any of the three
questions.explain: You are in the far right lane: from here you may go straight on (A) and turn right (B). To turn left, you must take up the far left position in advance, that is, the left lane, so path C is not allowed ⟦69⟧.

questions.q: There are no signs or markings that set lane directions. You are driving in the left lane. On which paths may you drive through the intersection?
options: Paths A and B
Path B only
Paths B and C
Any of the three
questions.explain: From the far left lane, you may go straight on (A) and turn left (B). Right turns are made only from the far right position, so turn C across the right lane is prohibited ⟦70⟧.

questions.q: You are turning left from the far left lane. Which path must you follow for the turn?
options: Path A
Either path
Path B
questions.explain: A turn is made into the lane that corresponds to the one you occupy: from the far left lane you must end up in the far left lane of the road you are turning onto (B). Path A takes you straight into the right lane ⟦71⟧.

questions.q: The markings permit a left turn from both lanes. You are turning left from the right lane. Which path must you follow?
options: Path A
Path B
Either path
questions.explain: You are in the second lane from the left, so after the turn you must also end up in the second lane from the left: that is A. The far left lane (B) is for those turning from the left lane at the same time as you ⟦72⟧.

questions.q: You are turning right from the far right lane. Which path must you follow for the turn?
options: Path B
Path A
Either path
questions.explain: From the far right lane, you turn into the far right lane of the new road (A). Path B takes you into the second lane, which no longer corresponds to the one you occupy ⟦73⟧.

questions.q: You are driving in the left lane. On which paths may you continue driving?
options: Path A only
Both paths
Path B only
Neither path
questions.explain: The arrow in the left lane permits only a left turn, and you must not go straight on from here: the right lane with the “straight ahead” arrow is intended for that ⟦74⟧.

questions.q: You are driving in the middle lane. On which paths may you continue driving?
options: Path B only
Paths A and B
Paths B and C
Any of the three
questions.explain: Sign 5.8.1 and the arrow in the middle lane permit only going straight on from that lane. Here, left turns are made from the left lane and right turns from the right lane ⟦75⟧.

questions.q: On your left there are tram tracks for the same direction, level with the carriageway. There are no signs 5.8.1 or 5.8.2. On which paths may you drive through the intersection from your lane?
options: Path B only
Paths B and C
Paths A and B
Any of the three
questions.explain: When there are such tram tracks on the left and signs 5.8.1 or 5.8.2 do not set lane directions, left turns and U-turns are made from the tram tracks. From your lane, you may go straight on (B) and turn right (C) ⟦76⟧.

questions.q: You need to turn left. On your left there are tram tracks for the same direction, level with the carriageway, and there are no signs 5.8.1 or 5.8.2. A tram is approaching from behind along the tracks. What should you do?
options: Turn left from your lane without entering the tracks
Enter the tracks ahead of the tram: the turning vehicle has priority
Turn left after the tram, directly from your lane
Let the tram go first, then enter the tracks and turn from them
questions.explain: Here, left turns are made from the tram tracks for the same direction, and the driver gives way to the tram ⟦77⟧. You must not drive onto the tracks right in front of it: let the tram go first, then move onto the tracks.

questions.q: You are turning left onto a road with reversible traffic. Which path must you follow for the turn?
options: Path B
Either path
Path A
questions.explain: When turning onto a road with reversible traffic, you must take the far right lane (A). The direction of traffic in the adjacent lane may change, so you may move to the left only after making sure that driving in your direction is permitted in that lane ⟦78⟧.

questions.q: You are making a U-turn at an intersection from the left lane, and there are no other vehicles nearby. On which path may you make the U-turn?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
questions.explain: A U-turn may be made with any turning radius, provided it is safe and does not impede others ⟦79⟧. Here, neither path impedes anyone.

questions.q: You are about to make a U-turn, and U-turns are not prohibited on this stretch. Which path must you take to start the manoeuvre?
options: Path B: first move into the left lane
Path A: make the U-turn directly from the right lane
Either path, if there is no oncoming traffic
questions.explain: Before a U-turn, the driver takes up the far left position on the carriageway in advance ⟦80⟧. So first move into the left lane (B); a U-turn from the right lane across the left lane is prohibited.

questions.q: You need to drive into a yard on the right. Which path should you take to start the manoeuvre?
options: Path A
Path B, then turn from the right lane
Either path, if the right lane is empty
questions.explain: You take up the far right position before a right turn not only at an intersection but also before entering a yard ⟦81⟧. First move into the right lane (B), and turn only from that lane.

questions.q: You need to turn into a yard on the left. Which path should you take to start the manoeuvre?
options: Path B, then turn from the left lane
Path A
Either path, if the left lane is empty
questions.explain: Before turning left, you must take up the far left position on the carriageway in advance ⟦82⟧. Turning from the right lane across the left lane is prohibited: first change lanes (B).

questions.q: On which path may you continue driving?
options: Path B only
Both paths
Neither path
Path A only
questions.explain: Sign 5.11.1 “U-turn place” marks a place where you may make a U-turn, but turning left there is prohibited. So only path A is allowed.

questions.q: On which path may you continue driving?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
questions.explain: You are at a stop: there is a shelter and sign 5.12. U-turns are prohibited at bus (tram) stops ⟦83⟧, so you may only go straight on. Make your U-turn further on, where it is permitted.

questions.q: On which path may you continue driving?
options: Path A only
Both paths
Path B only
questions.explain: Path A is a U-turn directly on the pedestrian crossing. U-turns are prohibited on pedestrian crossings ⟦84⟧, so you may only go straight on (B).

questions.q: You have driven past the house you need and want to reverse 20 m. There are no intersections, crossings or stops nearby, and nobody is behind you. On which paths may you continue driving?
options: Path A only
Path B only
Both paths
questions.explain: Reversing is permitted if the manoeuvre is safe and does not impede others, and here there is no intersection or other place where it is prohibited ⟦85⟧. So you may either reverse (A) or drive forward (B). When reversing, the reversing lights and hazard warning lights must be on ⟦86⟧.

questions.q: You and the driver of the green car are moving into the middle lane at the same time. Who must give way?
options: You
The one who switched on the indicator later
The one driving more slowly
The driver of the green car
questions.explain: You are in the right lane, and the green car is in the left lane. When changing lanes at the same time, the driver with the other car on the right gives way. You are on the green car's right, so its driver gives way ⟦87⟧.

questions.q: The driver of the blue car wants to move into your lane. Who goes first?
options: The blue car: it is slightly ahead of you
You

questions.explain: You are driving straight on in your lane, while the blue car is changing lanes. A driver changing lanes gives way to vehicles travelling in the same direction without changing direction, so you go first ⟦88⟧.

questions.q: You are accelerating in an acceleration lane and want to move into the main lane of an out-of-town road. Who goes first?
options: The blue car
You: the acceleration lane gives you priority
The one driving faster
questions.explain: You are in the acceleration lane, and the blue car is in the main lane of the road. From an acceleration lane, you move into the adjacent lane, giving way to vehicles travelling on that road ⟦89⟧.
